boundary_principles: A problem is owned by the earliest product promise it prevents, not by the live run that happened to expose it.
A case-transfer task may validate a shared Runtime but may not absorb unlimited shared-runtime redesign, provider qualification, release packaging or repository cleanup.
Engineering capability, coherent product output, research quality, owner acceptance and release qualification remain separate states.
An original acceptance clause that allows an honest block is terminal: it does not require unlimited repair until product pass.
Current-release hard integrity is not weakened. Unmet release gates remain blockers and may produce an honest blocked release decision.
Cross-case architecture consolidation is a new-version capability unless it is the smallest bounded change required to preserve an already accepted current-version path.
Paid exact-live is product proof, not the default integration test or field-by-field debugger.
